subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Energy Drinks and Modern Caffeine
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Energy Drinks and Modern Caffeine.

hook.text: Red Bull launched in 1987. By 2023, the global energy drink market exceeded $86 billion—and it's still growing.

buildup.text: Energy drinks combine caffeine (80–300 mg) with sugar, taurine, and B-vitamins in brightly packaged cans.

discovery.text: They target teens and young adults with extreme sports marketing—a demographic previously underserved by coffee culture.

twist.text: Emergency room visits linked to energy drinks more than doubled in four years. Heart arrhythmias are the leading concern.

climax.text: Countries including Denmark and France temporarily banned energy drinks. Others restrict sales to minors.

punchline.text: Same molecule, new packaging, bigger risks. Marketing outpaced science.

quiz.question: What is the main health concern with energy drinks?
options: Heart arrhythmias from high caffeine combined with other stimulants
